mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 1.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods matching the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs triggers a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 by more than 10,000 in a month
failure_condition: Across 20 triggered events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals weakening aggregate demand and corporate earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such INDPRO declines, SPX 60-day forward returns are not meaningfully lower than the prior 60-day average (median ratio > 1.02).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to anticipated rate hikes that discount future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 such inflation episodes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (median ratio ≤ 1.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for one month followed by two months of stability predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as markets anticipate the end of an over-tightening cycle.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% and remains ≥4.5% for two following months
failure_condition: During such UNRATE regimes, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than a neutral baseline (median ratio ≤ 1.015).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 5,000 units while industrial production remains flat or declining suggests resilient consumer demand, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 5,000 and INDPRO ≤ INDPRO previous month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: mixed demand signals with consumer resilience
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three months indicates a cooling inflationary bias, which is expected to produce a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such CPIAUCSL declines, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (median ratio ≤ 1.015).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of monthly new home sales (implied by INDPRO dynamics) to prior month falls by at least 20% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to housing market weakness and its spillover to corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO_t / INDPRO_(t-1) ≤ 0.8 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: sharp contraction in new home building
failure_condition: During such contractions, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (median ratio ≥ 1.01).
